articles.title: Raúl Varela: "¿Lamine? Raphinha es la verdadera estrella de este Barcelona"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu destaca el momento del brasileño y asegura que Yamal "aún está muy lejos del objetivo de ser ese 10 blaugrana que gana partidos y títulos por sí solo"
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu destaca el momento del brasileño y asegura que Yamal "aún está muy lejos del objetivo de ser ese 10 blaugrana que gana partidos y títulos por sí solo"
articles.body: Raphinha está un paso por delante de Lamine Yamal en este inicio de temporada. Así lo considera Raúl Varela, que en su editorial de La Tribu puso al brasileño como el gran referente actual del Barcelona pese al doblete del '10' frente al Rayo Vallecano. "Sea como fuere a Lamine, otra vez eclipsado por un imponente Raphinha, la verdadera estrella de este Barça, se le ve ya otra cara. Ya no está tan serio", aseguró Varela. Una situación que acompañó con una referencia a Andrés Montes: "Andrés Montes seguro que diría algo así como 'porque los jugones sonríen todos igual'". Lamine participó con dos goles en la victoria azulgrana frente al Rayo que coloca al Barça en el liderato compartido con el Real Madrid. "Lamine Yamal no quiso estropear la despedida de Leo Messi como internacional argentino, el principio de su final como futbolista en activo, y participó con un doblete, primeros goles desde aquel tanto mundialista ante Arabia, en la victoria del Barça frente al Rayo Vallecano que le aúpa al liderato compartido con el Real Madrid", explicó. El pleno azulgrana lleva a Varela a anticipar una dura pelea por el campeonato: "Tres partidos, tres victorias solventes y nueve puntazos que nos dirigen hacia una liga de cien como hace una década". Pese a recuperar la sonrisa y reencontrarse con el gol, Varela considera que Lamine afronta un curso importante para dar un paso adelante. "Es una temporada clave en su devenir. Todavía es joven, todavía le queda recorrido, pero el fútbol no para, no espera", señaló. El periodista también puso sobre la mesa la inevitable comparación con Leo Messi. "Después de un Campeonato del Mundo realmente discreto y aprovechando el inevitable paralelismo con Leo Messi, la realidad es que aún está muy lejos del objetivo de ser ese 10 blaugrana que gana partidos y títulos por sí solo", afirmó. Varela recordó además las palabras de Luis de la Fuente en Radio MARCA: "De la Fuente, padrino ayer en la botadura a las ondas de 'Otra Ronda', el nuevo programa nocturno de Radio Marca con el sello de nuestro querido 'Chitu', aseveró que el Messi español se llama Rodri Hernández a quien nadie coloca, como también le ocurre a Lamine, en la carrera recién estrenada por el Balón de Oro de pronóstico tan incierto este curso". El gran inicio del Barcelona coincide con el del Real Madrid en la segunda etapa de José Mourinho. "Esto no acaba más que comenzar y si ayer poníamos en valor a Bellingham o Mbappé, claves en el buen arranque de la segunda etapa de Mourinho, el Barça también aprieta el acelerador y quiere lo suyo", explicó Varela. Y volvió a destacar el peso de Raphinha en el conjunto azulgrana: "Raphinha hace de 9 y de lo que le pida Flick, Gordon sigue creciendo y sorprendiendo y la sonrisa de Lamine ya vuelve a dejarse ver por el Camp Nou el día que alcanzó la barrera de los 50 goles de culé". Varela cerró con una referencia irónica a la enorme distancia que todavía separa las cifras de Lamine de las de Messi: "Ya solo le quedan poco más de 600 en veinte años para empatar a Leo".

articles.title: Alberto Ávila se retira: "Ya no me quedan fuerzas ni motivación para seguir compitiendo al máximo nivel"
articles.standfirst: El atleta paralímpico, que tiene más de un millón de seguidores en Redes sociales y que participó en la última edición de Supervivientes, deja la competición
articles.summary: El atleta paralímpico, que tiene más de un millón de seguidores en Redes sociales y que participó en la última edición de Supervivientes, deja la competición
articles.body: Trece años de series que se hacían eternas, de cuerpo roto y ganas intactas. Trece años de maleta hecha y vuelta a hacer: cinco Mundiales, un subcampeonato de Europa, medallas en campeonatos de España absolutos en 100 y 200, y récords de España en 60, 100, 200 y 400 que ahí se quedan, aunque yo ya no esté en la pista para defenderlos". Así comienza Alberto Ávila el anuncio de su despedida en las redes sociales, donde cuenta con más de un millón de seguidores. El atleta paralímpico hizo historia recientemente al ser el primer concursante con discapacidad en 'Supervivientes', el reality que pone el cuerpo al límite. Ávila, uno de los concursantes más queridos, tuvo que abandonar el programa antes de tiempo por recomendación médica. El madrileño, que hasta ahora se entrenaba en las pistas del CAR de Madrid, reconoce que se marcha con una cuenta pendiente. "Hay una espina que sé que me va a acompañar siempre: quedarme fuera de París 2024. Duele. Y voy a ser sincero, porque siempre lo he sido con vosotros: duele más de lo que esperaba, y hay días en los que todavía me cuesta digerirlo", reconoce. Ávila explica los motivos por los que dice adiós a la competición, que no al deporte: "Llevo un tiempo escuchándome, y la verdad es que ya no me quedan fuerzas ni motivación para seguir compitiendo al máximo nivel. Y prefiero irme así, con la cabeza alta y agradecido, a arrastrarme por una pista que ya no me pide el cuerpo. Así que hoy me despido del atletismo de competición. De ESE Alberto, el de la pista. Gracias por sostenerme, romperme y reconstruirme mil veces. Gracias por enseñarme lo que valgo cuando ya no me quedaba nada dentro". El atleta paralímpico se despide de la competición de élite, pero no del deporte, que siempre formará parte de su vida y anticipa muchas más aventuras. "Esto no es un adiós al deporte, ni de coña (el deporte es mi droga, y ya sabéis que yo de las drogas no me desengancho). Vienen cosas nuevas: el canal de YouTube, “Cojo por el Mundo” sigue a tope, y hay aventuras deportivas nuevas cociéndose que os van a sorprender", dijo. Con la serie 'Cojo por el Mundo' pretende acabar con los estigmas hacia la discapacidad en otros países y cambiar mentalidades. "La pista me lo ha dado todo. Ahora toca ir a buscar el resto del mundo. Y sobre todo GRACIAS (así, en mayúsculas) a los que me habéis acompañado en mi camino. Esto no acaba, solo cambia de carril", finaliza.

articles.title: El "desastre bético" y la "vergüenza del Valencia", los mayores suspensos de la jornada
articles.standfirst: La Pizarra reparte las notas de la tercera fecha de Liga
articles.summary: La Pizarra reparte las notas de la tercera fecha de Liga
articles.body: La tercera jornada de LaLiga dejó mucho que analizar en La Pizarra. Miguel Quintana, Adrián Blanco y Álex de Llano repasaron lo mejor y lo peor del fin de semana, desde el mal momento de Betis y Valencia hasta las primeras victorias de Deportivo y Racing. El suspenso más rotundo de la jornada fue para el Betis, aunque "esta jornada podíamos haber puesto tres ceros". Los verdiblancos cayeron goleados en el Ciutat de Valencia. "Terrible defensa a balón parado, Bellerín estuvo fatal, falló prácticamente todo. Sin Álvaro Valles, quizá el Betis no hubiese sumado ninguna victoria", señaló Miguel Quintana. Adrián Blanco también fue muy crítico con el rendimiento verdiblanco: "Es un colapso a nivel defensivo muy bestia". El siguiente puesto fue para Matías Dituro por su actuación con el Elche, en la derrota ante el Racing. "Lió una traca gordísima en el gol de Zabiri. El Elche casi no puede competir el partido porque su portero se lo regaló. Dudo de que mida los riesgos. La clave es medir el riesgo", explicó Quintana. El Valencia tampoco salió bien parado de la jornada después de su actuación en Riazor. "Hasta su propio entrenador, Corberán, habló de vergüenza. El papel del Valencia en Riazor fue paupérrimo, no hubo reacción ni amor propio. Fue un papelón. No hay giro de tuerca. Corberán no es el culpable, pero esto no marcha", afirmó Quintana. Adrián Blanco lanzó una advertencia: "Cuidado con Corberán y el banquillo del Valencia, es un equipo sin alma, no transmite absolutamente nada". Álex de Llano añadió otro problema: "Se le suma la lesión de Sadiq. La situación no pinta demasiado bien". El arranque del Celta también genera dudas. "Ha arrancado con un 1 de 9, veo una falta de frescura alarmante. Hay para jugar bastante mejor", aseguró Quintana. De Llano coincidió: "Es un equipo demasiado plano. El equipo no mueve la pelota como antes, le está costando asociarse". Adrián, por su parte, señaló una ausencia: "Ante el Athletic eché en falta a Borja Iglesias". Más confianza existe alrededor del Villarreal pese a su inicio. "No es el comienzo ideal, pero es circunstancial, no estoy preocupado. Aunque tiene mucho sentido lo de Iñigo Pérez, hay un cambio respecto a lo que hacía Marcelino. Esto llevará tiempo. Nivel de preocupación con el Celta, un ámbar. Con el Villarreal, un verde. Y con el Valencia, un stop", valoró Quintana. Adrián también confía en el proyecto: "Tiene un plantillón y ha fichado un entrenadorazo. Pero el calendario no afloja y empieza la Champions". El aprobado llegó para Osasuna. "Su inicio es muy bueno pero el juego tampoco está siendo brillante. Siete puntos de nueve, solo un gol encajado, es un equipo sólido, que no se regala, que no trenza demasiadas jugadas brillantes, pero que está siendo efectivo. Es lo que se esperaba de Luis Miguel Ramis", explicó Quintana. Adrián lo definió como un "equipo solvente, al que no le importa ceder la iniciativa", mientras que De Llano destacó al técnico: "Ramis, por el momento, lo está haciendo muy bien". El Barcelona continúa dejando buenas sensaciones, especialmente por su costado izquierdo. "Raphinha está brutal. Me gustó mucho la banda que está comenzando a compartir Xavi Espart y Gordon. Me está gustando mucho el Barça en general y la banda izquierda en particular", aseguró Quintana. Adrián destacó especialmente a Xavi Espart: "Da gusto cómo está jugando Xavi Espart, es muy hábil, muy bueno técnicamente, entiende muy bien el juego". De Llano añadió: "Flick está invirtiendo mucho en Espart". El notable fue compartido por Atlético y Real Madrid. "Un siete compartido para Atleti y Madrid por sus primeras mitades. Me encantó la movilidad ofensiva del Atleti y el Madrid demostró su superioridad contra el Málaga", afirmó Quintana. Para Adrián fueron "dos notables para Madrid y Atleti y muchas lecturas positivas. El Atleti puede hacer estos partidos fuera de casa. El Madrid parece un equipo más comprometido". De Llano puso el foco en un nombre propio: "Para enmarcar el partido de Baena, me fascinó". La jornada también dejó el pleno del fútbol vasco. Quintana destacó la "victoria del Alavés ante el Villarreal con un gran Ángel Pérez, es un torbellino; el triunfo de la Real ante el Espanyol con un enorme Oyarzabal, impecable en los registros; y la victoria del Athletic ante el Celta, demostrando ser un equipo nuevo. Me está gustando bastante más de lo que dice la clasificación". De Llano añadió: "Terzic tiene trabajo por delante, pero los cimientos parecen sólidos". Bardeli y Olasagasti fueron dos de los grandes protagonistas del Levante. "Buen partido de muchos jugadores del Levante. Bardeli y Olasagasti destrozaron el centro del campo del Betis. Fueron el motor ofensivo de un Levante que, por fin, carburó. Fueron claves en la victoria y goleada granota", explicó Quintana. Adrián destacó a Olasagasti: "En el caso de Olasa, agradecemos jugar por dentro y con capacidad para llegar". La máxima nota fue compartida por Deportivo y Racing después de conseguir sus primeras victorias. "Un diez compartido para la primera victoria del Depor y del Racing. Lo de Aubameyang, con los tres goles, es una barbaridad. El Valencia exigió poco, pero me gustó el Depor", explicó Quintana. Adrián también destacó la actuación deportivista: "Gran actuación del Depor, Riazor acompañó. Aubameyang está pletórico. Ojalá se mantenga así". Sobre el Racing, Quintana destacó la "gran actuación de Zabiri, fue una pesadilla para Dituro y para el Elche". De Llano puso en valor su impacto inmediato: "Zabiri acaba de llegar y en 36 minutos marca un hat trick, es muy importante".

articles.title: Derby classic coming as Hearts belief grows
articles.summary: Whenever opposition fans fall over themselves to launch into a snide rendition of Joy Division's biggest hit and chant, 'Hearts are falling apart', it tends...
articles.body:
Whenever opposition fans fall over themselves to launch into a snide rendition of Joy Division's biggest hit and chant, 'Hearts are falling apart', it tends to feel a little premature.

Our rivals may have gleefully watched us lose our first four competitive games, but Hearts have since responded with back-to-back league victories, earn a favourable away draw in the League Cup quarter-final and progress to the Conference League league phase - restoring a little national pride in the coefficient along the way.

Conveniently, 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' isn't the most requested song in the jukebox in Leith or Aberdeen pubs these past few weeks.

Some players and managers can spend an entire Hearts career without producing one defining memory. Yet only a couple of months in, Wouter Vrancken and several of his players already have their 'maroon moment' after the penalty shootout victory over Rapid in Vienna.

Down to 10 men, with two out-and-out wingers and a striker still on the pitch, Vrancken responded to Blair Spittal's injury by sending on attacker Rogers Mato for the 30 minutes of extra time. It was one of the boldest tactical gambles I can remember from a Hearts manager.

Thankfully, fortune favoured the brave. Hearts earned their reward at the end of a nerve-shredding shootout, with Beau Reus producing two excellent saves to swing it our way.

Calvin Miller's night in Vienna will be remembered for years. It was a talismanic display; he switched positions several times, finished the game hobbling in central midfield and scored one of the most iconic European goals in the club's history.

Six league-phase games now await, including former European heavyweights Monaco at home. Admittedly, that fixture might have been even more alluring on the Cote d'Azur, but I'm sure our visitors will appreciate the dreich Edinburgh weather in November.

The Petroclub debacle from a couple of seasons ago showed that seven points do not guarantee progression to the knockout stage. Even so, if Hearts continue on this upward trajectory under Vrancken, I fancy us to take three wins from these fixtures. And, as Benfica away demonstrated, this side does not play for stalemates.

Excluding that late collapse at Pittodrie in the opening game of the season, there's a growing confidence with supporters in this Hearts side, so much so that St Johnstone's late rally last Saturday didn't spook too many supporters inside Tynecastle as we eeked out a 2-1 win to go into third in the Scottish Premiership.

A Thursday evening Edinburgh derby will feel strange, although European commitments mean both sides are becoming accustomed to midweek football. As long as most of Easter Road is as despondent at full-time as it was after the defeat by Gent, I'll be delighted.

Hearts' recent league record at Easter Road is almost evenly divided between wins, draws and defeats. Across the past 25 meetings there, we have won eight, Hibs have won 10 and seven have ended level.

History puts our chances of victory at roughly one in three, but I have a feeling a classic is coming. Both defences look vulnerable; Hearts have conceded in eight of the past nine games and Hibs in seven of their past 10. I'm going for a 3-2 Hearts win.

European progression has restored the belief; victory at Easter Road would confirm this Hearts side is no longer falling apart, but coming together at exactly the right time.

articles.title: Mud, flippers and snorkels: Wales celebrates 40 years of bog racing
articles.summary: Competitors have plunged into a Welsh peat bog for the 40th World Bog Snorkelling Championships. The unusual event in Llanwrtyd Wells combines snorkels, flip...
articles.body:
The August bank holiday weekend in Britain is often the opportunity for many to take part in unusual activities and this year lived up to expectations.

For mud-lovers in Wales, that meant a day spent at the World Bog Snorkelling Championships which celebrated its 40th anniversary in Llanwrtyd Wells.

Competitors raced through a peat bog using snorkels, with flippers permitted but conventional swimming strokes banned.

The event, which began as a tourism initiative, continues to attract participants and spectators to the rural Welsh town, offering an unusual test of endurance, technique and a right old laugh.

articles.body:

Games Played / Games Started – 10 games played – 1 started

Stats – 18 receptions for 243 yards and 5 carries for 18 yards and a TD.

Townsend comes to Purdue from a pretty good Iowa State program. He played in 10 of their games last season and grabbed 18 catches. He also rushed the ball five times. So 23 touches over 10 games. Not exactly the go to guy, but in this modern world of college football sometimes you've gotta look a little deeper. Prior to Iowa State Townsend spent three seasons at UCF. He redshirted during his junior season so to get a true look at what he can do we have to go back to his sophomore season. He appeared in 11 games and started 10 with 33 receptions for 325 yards and 3 TDs plus 15 rushes for 163 yards. If Purdue can get that kind of production out of Townsend I think they'll be very happy.

High School : Heritage Hills High School

Stats – 40 tackles, eight TFL, three sacks, one interception, one FF

Recruiting Rankings – 3* recruit. Number 1 safety in the state of Indiana. Number 8 recruit in Indiana. Mr Football Runner-up.

This is how I know I'm getting old. I saw Jett Goldsberry and said to myself, "hmmm I wonder if that's Jon Goldsberry's younger brother. I'll google it because it has to be. (proceeds to Google) Oh no, it's his son!" Yeah that's right, Purdue continues to get the children of players I remember watching. Jon finished his time at Purdue in 2004, my freshman year. Exceuse me while I go turn into dust. As for Jett, he's every bit the athlete that his father was. You can see his speed and strength in the highlights above, there's plenty more on Hudl if you're interested and have some time. Goldsberry will likely struggle to get on the field as a DB this season, but that's no slight on him. In his first year with the program he will need to learn the schemes, get adjusted to college life, and hop in the weight room as all true freshman do. With the new NCAA rules and the elimination of redshirting it wouldn't suprise me to see him out on the field toward the end of the game against Indiana State or on special teams throughout the year. He's a solid athlete and Purdue will need to take advantage of every athlete on the roster.

Good luck to both young men this season!

articles.title: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova, 16, wins first set but falls to Olympic gold medalist at US Open
articles.summary: Kristina Liutova of Redmond, 16, won the first set against 2024 Olympic gold medalist Zheng Qinwen but couldn’t hold off the veteran, falling in the first ro...
articles.body:
Kristina Liutova of Redmond, 16, won the first set against 2024 Olympic gold medalist Zheng Qinwen but couldn't hold off the veteran, falling in the first round of the US Open on Monday, 4-6, 6-3, 6-1.

Liutova left the court in tears after her nine-match winning streak came to an end.

ESPN match commentator Robbie Koenig offered words of encouragement for Liutova.

I'll tell you what, there will be a lot more tears of joy in the years to come," Koenig said. "That's for sure, given the game that she possesses. Don't worry about that, Kristina."

First player born in the 2010s to reach a Grand Slam main draw

Liutova had to fight her way through three qualifying matches to earn a spot in the main draw.

"[She's] just so accurate with her ball striking," Koenig said of Liutova early in Monday's match. "I'm gobsmacked that she's just 16 years of age."

Liutova is the first player born in the 2010s to qualify for the main draw of a Grand Slam tournament and was the youngest person in the draw. In early August, she became the first person born in that decade to win a WTA title with her victory at the Memphis Classic.

"Honestly, I never look at the stats," Liutova told KIRO Newsradio before the US Open. "When I get told, I forget immediately."

Zheng calls Liutova's tennis 'incredible'

Zheng acknowledged the teenager in her post-match interview on ESPN.

"I want to say congratulations first to the opponent because she's only 16 years old," Zheng said. "Very young junior, and she played incredible tennis. Fights a lot. It was not easy for me."

Two comeback stories collide at the US Open

Zheng, like Liutova, had to play the qualifying rounds of the US Open this year. But in 2023 and 2024, she made the US Open quarterfinals.

In 2024, she reached the Australian Open final and the French Open quarterfinals in 2025. But in the summer of 2025, Zheng underwent arthroscopic elbow surgery.

As she recovered from surgery, her ranking fell. But like Liutova, her ranking is now on the rise.

Liutova takes home $140,000 — and dreams of taking care of mom

Liutova will take home $140,000 in prize money for qualifying for the first round at the US Open.

While training in Redmond earlier this month, Liutova told KIRO Newsradio she wants to take care of her mom.

"I want to make sure that she's happy, and in the future she has an easy life — a house, a cat — and just watch my matches with no worries and no pressure," Liutova said. "My goals and dreams are hers; hers are mine."

This story was originally posted on MyNorthwest.com

articles.title: Time for McCann to take blinkers off and change system
articles.summary: Neil McCann was nippy to BBC Scotland's Jonathan Sutherland after the cup win over Ayr United when asked about our propensity for losing goals.  It's time fo...
articles.body:
I was going to write this column on Saturday night after the Dundee United game but I simply couldn't find enough swear words to describe our performance.

Neil McCann was nippy to BBC Scotland's Jonathan Sutherland after the cup win over Ayr United when asked about our propensity for losing goals.

It's time for him to take the blinkers off and accept what all Killie fans can see - his system simply isn't working.

Our defence is hugely exposed when we lose the ball in the opposition half and they can break on us at will.

I feel sorry for the players who are being told to play a system they don't look comfortable with.

It's time to ditch the two up top and get an extra body in the middle of the park to offer some protection. Joe Hugill is fine playing the lone striker role and we can introduce some width that will also offer some cover to the full-backs.

We have three games in the next ten days starting with St Mirren on Wednesday night, a game we simply must win.

One or two more heavy defeats and McCann could find himself back in a studio shouting at Tom English.

Sandy Armour is editor of The Killie Hippo fanzine

articles.title: Broadcaster forced to apologise over Jazz Chisholm Jr. comments after Yankees win over Red Sox
articles.summary: Boston radio broadcaster Will Flemming has been forced to apologise after his outburst towards New York Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. The Yankees ended...
articles.body:
Boston radio broadcaster Will Flemming has been forced to apologise after his outburst towards New York Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.

The Yankees ended their series against the Boston Red Sox with a resounding 16-1 victory over the weekend.

During the latter stages of the game at Yankee Stadium, Chisholm was heavily criticised for stealing second and third base despite being so far ahead.

"Wouldn't you sort of like to see Moran drill Wells here? That's a selfish play. That's just padding your stats. That's who Jazz is," said Flemming during the broadcast.

The comments have seen significant backlash, with the broadcaster forced into making an apology through his social media channels in the days since.

What Will Flemming said in public apology to Yankees infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr.

Chisholm has hit 18 home runs this season, but he was unable to add another to his name in the emphatic 16-1 victory on Sunday.

It has not been a straightforward season for the second baseman, who has received some criticism over recent weeks.

Responding to the comments he made during his live broadcast, Flemming shared the following statement on X.

"Since I have been receiving nonstop calls and threats, I felt like it was important to hop back on here and say: My comments during yesterday's broadcast crossed a line. I'm emotional and a fan at heart and that bled into the broadcast," he said.

"I meant no disrespect to the Yankees players or organization. I could and should have used different words. These rivalry games get me fired up; I apologize for letting the emotion of the moment get the best of me."

Although it is clear that Flemming should not have said what he said, the reaction from some fans has certainly stepped over the line.

Chisholm actually responded to the comments himself, with the Yankees infielder laughing off Flemming's words.

"I didn't even know who that was until this morning, and I'm still not going to remember who he is after today," he said.

Hopefully, now an apology has been made, this can all be swept under the rug and everyone can move on.

articles.title: Colchester sign Blackpool forward Kouassi
articles.summary: Colchester United sign Blackpool forward Kylian Kouassi for an undisclosed fee, on a two-year deal.
articles.body:
Colchester United have signed Blackpool forward Kylian Kouassi for an undisclosed fee.

The 23-year-old had been with the Seasiders since 2023, but spent the last two seasons on loan at Salford City and Cambridge United.

articles.title: 'We have a common goal': Kompany on Klopp visit
articles.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has said he and Jürgen Klopp have "a common goal" as he talked about a weekend visit to Munich of the new German national...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has said he and Jürgen Klopp have "a common goal" as he talked about a weekend visit to Munich of the new German national team helmsman.

Kompany said on Tuesday that he had "a very interesting" exchange with Klopp: "50% was about the time we played against each other and 50% was about the future."

Kompany was up against former Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool coach Klopp as a player for SV Hamburg and Manchester City and then as Burnley coach.

"It's interesting to have a chat with a coach who's no longer involved in the day-to-day training work but who has a wealth of experience. I've seen what he's done and the successes he's had. It's interesting to hear how he went about it and achieved it," Kompany said.

Klopp was appointed in succession of Julian Nagelsmann who resigned after Germany's round of 32 exit at the World Cup.

Klopp will announce his first squad on September 17 for four Nations League group matches against the Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (twice), with a number of Bayern players expected to be picked.

"In my experience, the relationship between the club and the national team isn't a difficult one. We have a common goal," Kompany said.

"Germany must qualify; that's clear, and for that you need the best players.

"You win tournaments in the summer - so the players need to be fit and available. So that Germany can achieve something special and perhaps lose to Belgium in the final," he quipped in reference to his home country.

Klopp attended Bayern's Bundesliga season opener on Friday against VfB Stuttgart, whose training he has since also visited, and he named Bayern's appointment of Kompany in 2024 "courageous but super smart.

"He was a world class player and is on his way to becoming a world class coach," Klopp said.

articles.title: Fabio Vieira signs for Hamburg
articles.summary: Hamburg have secured the midfielder after declining their original purchase option, with the eventual terms leaving Arsenal’s negotiating position open to sc...
articles.body:
Hamburg have secured the midfielder after declining their original purchase option, with the eventual terms leaving Arsenal's negotiating position open to scrutiny.

Fabio Vieira has completed a permanent move from Arsenal to Hamburger SV , ending his four-year association with the club after the Bundesliga side returned for him following last season's loan spell.

The agreement is worth about €10 million, or £8.6 million, after Hamburg decided not to activate the €22 million purchase option contained in Vieira's loan deal.

The German club instead continued negotiations, consistently offering a substantially lower figure and have ultimately secured the midfielder for the amount the said they would pay all summer.

There had been widespread doubt that HSV would pay the option amount at the time of the loan, and those doubts proved justified when the Bundesliga side declined to exercise the clause.

Hamburg nevertheless remained determined to keep Vieira and made clear that they wanted to pay no more than €10 million.

Initial indications from Arsenal were that they expected considerably more and intended to take a firm position in negotiations, but the final agreement has been struck at about €10 million.

The final structure of the transfer will determine how Arsenal's negotiations are ultimately judged. If the agreement contains add-ons or a sell-on clause, those provisions could increase the value of the deal beyond the initial €10 million. It still won't come close to that original option, however.

Without such extras, Arsenal have accepted essentially the figure Hamburg were prepared to offer earlier in the summer. That would represent a disappointing outcome for a club attempting to improve its record of extracting value from outgoing players.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. could not hide his emotions while talking about surviving Giants’ cut day
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. shared a candid response when asked about his feelings on being named to the New York Giants’ 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. shared a candid response when asked about his feelings on being named to the New York Giants' 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season.

OBJ spent all of the 2025 season on the sidelines, missing half the year with a PED suspension and then waiting until the 2026 preseason for the Giants to give him a prove-it, non-guaranteed camp deal.

He earned his spot on the final 53-man roster to keep his NFL career alive through pure hard work, earning a spot under coach John Harbaugh despite no prior relationship with the coach.

Odell Beckham Jr. opens up on the emotions after receiving Giants contract

Beckham Jr. spoke to the media after the Giants' final roster was confirmed with him on it, with the WR sharing an emotional response discussing what it means to him and his family.

"I had those tears when I got back to the hotel after figuring out that I am going to be here and that I have an opportunity to rewrite some of the last chapter. Don't know, last year or whatever it is, but I definitely had that moment where it was like, you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I've went through. It was very healing, very emotional, but something I am happy about."

OBJ will join a competent WR room on the Giants, likely featuring as a rotational depth piece behind the likes of Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney, Malachi Fields, and Darius Slayton.

The 33-year-old WR made it clear that he doesn't know if this season will be his last in the NFL, but if he can have a productive year on the field, he might generate more interest next season.

OBJ is a notable member of the Giants' recent history, playing 59 career games for them between 2014 and 2018. He had 390 receptions for 5,476 receiving yards and 44 touchdowns for the franchise.

That production is no longer feasible for Beckham Jr., but if he can have productive moments as a veteran WR under coach Harbaugh, he could add another year to his NFL career.

His emotions about making the team are justified, as he could only do it on pure skill and effort after the controversies surrounding him in recent years. He earned his redemption, and now has to deliver on it.

articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic is already considered one of the league's best guards, especially after winning the scoring title last season. He still has a long way to go in his NBA career, but Lance Stephenson already believes Doncic is among the best floor generals in league history.

"Isiah Thomas. This is not in order. Magic Johnson. Jason Kidd. Stephen Curry. That's four? I got Luka," Stephenson said on the 3's and Ones podcast.

"Right now, it is. But I agree, if he stays at this pace, Luka is top-five ever. Yeah, for sure," added American music artist Russ to double down on Stephenson's take.

At 27 years old, Doncic has already achieved a lot in his career, including six All-Star selections, six All-NBA First Team selections, two scoring titles, and one Western Conference Finals MVP, among others. As he approaches his third year with the Los Angeles Lakers, Doncic is expected to carry the team, especially with LeBron James no longer around.

Los Angeles Lakers News: Ziaire Williams relishes opportunity to play alongside Luka Doncic

With LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers, the Los Angeles Lakers made it a point to surround Luka Doncic with athleticism, which is why they signed Ziaire Williams to a one-year contract.

In an exclusive interview with Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register, Williams detailed his upcoming role for the Los Angeles Lakers this year.

"Obviously Luka (Doncic) and AR (Austin Reaves) are going to be the main primary ball handlers," Williams stated. "So just playing off them, being able to shoot, cut, make plays in transition, stuff like that. They thought it was a great fit for me to be here, and the feeling was mutual."

"I can tell (Doncic's) leadership. He wants to step up even more this year. I'm excited, man. I'm really excited to play with him. And of course, when we're playing basketball, it's just he makes the game just so easy and looks so simple. He's going to make my life a lot easier for sure," he added.

Ja Morant is out to redeem himself this upcoming season when he suits up for the Portland Trail Blazers , and according to former NBA forward Stephen Jackson, the 27-year-old guard can use this opportunity to re-establish himself as one of the league's top stars.

"I'm happy for him. I up a million times and kept getting chances. So, I'm glad he understands. Well, I want him to understand that it's not what you do, it's what you do after. You got the opportunity to fix all this by coming out averaging 18-20, having a great year," Jackson said of Morant via the All the Smoke podcast.

"If he comes out this year and averages 18 to 20, he doesn't really have the pressure because you got Dame there. You got Avdija who's really their number one option. You just come out and get back to doing what you love and having fun. You know, you get out of Memphis; this is a great opportunity to kind of reclaim who you are," he continued.

This past season, Morant averaged 19.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 8.1 assists on a subpar 41.0 percent shooting across 20 regular-season games for the Memphis Grizzlies. He was eventually traded to the Portland Trail Blazers in exchange for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray – a return deemed too low for Memphis, considering Morant's star power.

Portland Trail Blazers News: Insider says the quiet part out loud about Nike's involvement in the Ja Morant trade

According to Brandon "Scoop B" Robinson, Nike, based in Beaverton, Oregon, played a significant role in moving Ja Morant to the Portland Trail Blazers this offseason.

"Nike wants to keep an eye on him because they have a ton invested in him," an anonymous source told Robinson. "From the Morant and Nike side, this will give him a chance to resurrect his career. We want him to change his image a little bit, but we still want him to be his authentic self."

"For Nike, this is a strategic risk-management move, allowing their top executives, marketing teams, and player relations reps to protect their massive financial investment in real-time while ensuring Morant stays true to the raw authenticity that made him a global icon," he added.

articles.title: Debunking Report About Jonathan Kuminga’s Reason For Snubbing The Lakers
articles.summary: Jonathan Kuminga has not spoken about why he rejected the Lakers.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers wanted to add Jonathan Kuminga to their ranks in this post- LeBron James era, but he snubbed them and headed to the Minnesota Timberwolves in free agency. It was an interesting decision, and Kuminga's agent, Aaron Turner, has had a lot to say about his client choosing the Timberwolves .

Kuminga himself hasn't, but some quotes attributed to him surfaced on social media recently. In them, the 23-year-old talked about Los Angeles not being the right environment for him and that the expectations surrounding the Lakers can serve as a distraction.

To no one's surprise, these quotes went viral, but Kuminga never said any of this. An X user named Marc Jacobs posted these online, citing The Athletic as the source.

"Not to come off disrespectful, but I didn't feel like Los Angeles was the right environment for me. There's a level of expectation and outside noise surrounding the Lakers that can become distracting, and I wanted a situation where I could stay focused on basketball and my development. I also felt Minnesota offered a better defensive fit and a clearer role for me. Ultimately, it was the better situation."

The Athletic hasn't published these quotes anywhere, however. This is fabrication likely done with the intent of farming engagement. This isn't the first time Jacobs has done it either. The Athletic's Dan Woike called him out in August for some fake Luka Doncic quotes he had posted and claimed were from The Athletic.

"This is 10000 percent false and not something that Luka said or something that appeared in The Athletic – where is the "parody" in just being a liar," Woike wrote.

In a now-deleted post, Jacobs had shared Doncic's reaction to James leaving the Los Angeles Lakers .

"Obviously, LeBron did a lot for this team and made us better," Jacobs wrote. "We have a lot of respect for everything he brought to Los Angeles, but I think the team we have now fits us really well. We added a lot of guys who can defend, shoot, and make plays, and I really like the balance of this group. I think we have a better chance to compete at the highest level and ultimately win."

Jacobs deleted the post after getting called out by Woike. He might do the same this time around as well. It's a shame just how often these fake quotes get posted online nowadays. These are quite damaging not only to the players, but also to the publications.

If you want to know why Kuminga, who averaged 12.2 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 0.6 steals, and 0.3 blocks per game for the Golden State Warriors and the Atlanta Hawks in 2025-26, signed a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Timberwolves, all you have to do is listen to his agent.

Turner has spoken about rejecting bigger offers from teams like the Lakers . They had put a three-year deal worth $12 million-plus annually on the table, but Kuminga and Turner believe the Timberwolves are the right fit.

articles.summary: Charlton Athletic midfielder Jodie Hutton says that the club’s primary target this season is to stay in the Barclays Women’s Super League.The Addicks were pr...
articles.body:
Charlton Athletic midfielder Jodie Hutton says that the club's primary target this season is to stay in the Barclays Women's Super League.

The Addicks were promoted to the top tier after defeating Leicester City on penalties in a one-off play-off tie back in May.

Charlton Athletic were Barclays WSL2 leaders for most of the season but ended up needing to win the play-off to seal promotion. When speaking in a Charlton Athletic media session, midfielder Hutton said that the players showed their togetherness in finally getting over the line.

"We had a good season from the start," Hutton said. "It comes from off the pitch, we are a very together team. It didn't end how we wanted, going into the play-offs but after the Birmingham game, we just wanted to get on with it. We knew we had one more chance and we took it.

"It came down to togetherness and being on the same wavelength. It was good to get the win in the play-offs."

Charlton Athletic go into their first Barclays Women's Super League season as one of the relegation favourites. Hutton said that the South East Londoners' target this season is very clear.

She said "If we are being honest, it's to stay in the league. We are not going to say that we are targeting the top end of the table because everybody knows that's unrealistic.

"We know that it's going to be hard, so our main aim is to stay in the league and compete. Hopefully, we will do that."

Charlton Athletic are known for their defensive qualities. Hutton says that The Addicks will look to bring those attributes to the Barclays Women's Super League whilst continuing to thrive on an underdog mentality.

She said "We are quite a defensive team, we had to play on the counter attack [last season] and I think that'll help us going into the WSL.

"We are going in as the underdogs, just like we did last year and we kind of like that because we want to prove people wrong.

"We've been working on our defending. Last year, we were a defensive team and that will help because we are used to that."

Charlton Athletic kick-off the new Barclays Women's Super League season with a home fixture against Liverpool on Sunday.

articles.title: Commanders GM Adam Peters unfairly criticized for one specific comment
articles.summary: It’s fair to judge Peters on his personnel decisions, but some fans were upset with one comment he made on Monday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders general manager met with the media on Monday to discuss the offseason, the roster and the season ahead. One thing Peters said didn't sit right with some.

"Obviously our fans are passionate, and you love to have passionate fans; that's great," Peters said on Monday. "But there's a lot of stuff we're doing here that maybe they don't see, and a lot of things I'm excited to see in a couple of weeks. We couldn't be more thrilled than to start our season where we're starting it, and it's going to be a great challenge, and we're looking forward to it."

Reading X (formerly Twitter), this Peters' quote did not go over too well. However, I did not interpret Peters' comment as an arrogant professor condescendingly talking down to students he believes are ignorant.

Sometimes we have to remind ourselves when reading literature or listening to a speech, and yes, even in a press conference, "What is the immediate context in which this reply is being spoken?" In other words, one can't simply read an answer and foolishly make a conclusion accurately or reliably unless you recognize the question to which the speaker is responding.

In this case, one inquired, "AP, this one is for you. Simply judging by the tenor and the tone from the fan base over the past week, there's certainly some worry there. My question to you is, 'What gives you hope that you know everything's going to be all right basically with this team, the structure, going forward?'

AP visibly was not thrilled with that question. First of all, there are extremists in every fan base. Some are extremely negative, extremely pessimistic, most is doom and gloom for these people.. Frankly, they are emotionally unreliable people. Then there are fans who are extremely naive and optimistic, never questioning when they should. So how was Peters supposed to respond to how extreme fanatics are venting on social media?

Peters responded by referring back to Quinn's previous response. Peters echoed what Quinn had said about his two new coordinators, to Jayden Daniels having a very good training camp. Peters expressed he is confident in the coaching staff. He also knows their defensive personnel will be better in 2026.

So yes, Peters knows more, much more than the fan base. Yes, he sees more, hears more, interacts more. It's all true. He wasn't being condescending at all on Monday. Now, having said all of that, neither Peters nor any GM should get a free pass. They should all be judged by their personnel moves and their drafts. It's part of the business. I am confident Peters thinks much more about his three drafts for the Commanders than any fans do.

Don't you think Peters certainly knows what is at stake for this team coming off of a 5-12 season?

articles.title: Former NFL Wide Receiver Damoun Patterson Booked on Grand Theft and Armed Burglary Charges
articles.summary: Former NFL wide receiver Damoun Patterson has gone from catching passes on Sundays to facing a list of felony charges following an arrest in Daytona Beach, F...
articles.body:
Former NFL wide receiver Damoun Patterson has gone from catching passes on Sundays to facing a list of felony charges following an arrest in Daytona Beach, Florida. The Daytona Beach Police Department says Patterson was taken into custody in connection with an incident involving a vehicle, a deadly weapon, and a residence.

Patterson spent time with several NFL organizations during his professional football career, including the Pittsburgh Steelers, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and New England Patriots. Now, the former receiver has found himself on the other side of a Daytona Beach Police Department arrest announcement.

According to police, Patterson was booked on charges that include Grand Theft of a Motor Vehicle, Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon, Criminal Mischief, and Armed Burglary of a Dwelling. The department did not provide additional details about what led up to the incident in its social media post.

Still, that's quite a collection of charges attached to what was once a familiar name on NFL rosters. Footage shared by Daytona Beach police offers a closer look at the circumstances surrounding Patterson's arrest and the encounter that landed him behind bars.

Please give the following video a moment to load.

The clip posted to the Daytona Beach Police Department's Facebook page features officers approaching a vehicle before cutting to Patterson's arrest. Additional footage adds context to the events after the arrest, which show Patterson cooperating with officers, and even talking to them about his past football career at one point.

Even though some of the officers seemed genuinely interested, the fact of the matter is that he is still being wanted for various felonies. One officer explained to Patterson that he was going to be taken to prison that evening, but that he was likely also going to be contacted by the Orlando Police Department for previous issues.

Regardless of everything that he is being accused of, he seemed to accept his fate and did everything asked of him by the police who were on the scene. Honestly, that's likely what helped make the whole scenario far less of a big deal than it actually is to those who live in the area since it looks like the events are happening in some sort of neighborhood.

Whatever ultimately comes of the case, Patterson is facing several serious accusations following his arrest. Armed burglary and aggravated assault with a deadly weapon sit alongside the grand theft and criminal mischief charges listed by Daytona Beach police.

The department's announcement does not specify what weapon Patterson is accused of possessing, whose vehicle was involved, or the extent of the property damage behind the criminal mischief charge. Those details will likely become clearer as the case moves through the judicial process.

For now, the former NFL receiver has traded his name appearing on football rosters for one appearing in a Daytona Beach police report. Patterson has been booked on the listed charges, though as the department itself emphasized, he is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

articles.title: Everything comes down to what’s happening in the trenches for Notre Dame
articles.summary: The that Marcus Freeman wants to field at Notre Dame is probably the team that Marcus Freeman HAS at Notre Dame.
articles.body:
Marcus Freeman took the podium on Monday to begin the first game week for Notre Dame this season as the Irish travel to Green Bay to take on the Wisconsin Badgers in the Shamrock Series. While his press conference didn't offer too many revelations about this 2026 Notre Dame team, I paid particular attention to anything that was discussed about the offensive and defensive lines.

Marcus Freeman has long talked about the Irish being an offensive and defensive line driven team. Despite Wisconsin being a bit down in recent years, you still look at them as a program that does the work in the trenches as well as anyone.

For Notre Dame, the offensive line has been a work in progress since this spring, and now we have the fuller picture. Ashton Craig is back from injury, which not only makes the center position stronger and deeper with Joe Otting backing him up, it also means there won't be a possible move to guard (which was a thing during fall camp).

"He's coming off an ACL injury, but he has a lot of experience. There's a calmness he brings. He's a really, really good football player and has progressed throughout camp with his workload. He's ready to go. There's a lot of confidence we have in Joe Otting, but having Ashton out there will help our offense."

The biggest battle on the offensive line was probably at right guard. At first it was between Sullivan Absher and Matty Augustine, but a foot injury to Augustine made things murkier. This is when the talk about Craig possibly moving to guard started to come about, but little by little, Styles Prescod started to make a push — and it's still up in the air this week. While the indecision may come off as a bad thing, it really does seem more like an embarrassment of riches situation. Notre Dame's offensive line will be really good this year regardless of this one position battle.

"Sullivan Absher and Styles Prescod are an "or" at right guard on the depth chart." "We have to make a decision soon. We're not making it today…We feel confident at the right guard position. You might see them both. It's a credit to the progression Styles has made in training camp."

"Sullivan Absher and Styles Prescod are an "or" at right guard on the depth chart."

"We have to make a decision soon. We're not making it today…We feel confident at the right guard position. You might see them both. It's a credit to the progression Styles has made in training camp."

Going over to the defensive side of the trenches, perhaps the biggest surprise of all was Armel Mukam locking down THE starting job at defensive tackle.

"He's at the facility early and stays late. He does a lot to be the best football player he can be. He's improved and has worked tirelessly with Coach Partridge. He's grasped the information from Coach Partridge…I'm proud of him. I'm grateful that he's in our program. He's done a terrific job since he's been back."

Notre Dame almost lost Mukam to the transfer portal, but they were able to bring him back. With the additions of guys like Francis Brewu and Tionne Gray, the return of Mukam wasn't viewed as a huge deal — but it really was.

And all of that is just part of the story when it comes to the trenches for the Irish. What's clear, however, is that this team is becoming exactly what Marcus Freeman wants, and that's the type of team which can win a national championship.

articles.title: NFL Insider Believes Kevin O’Connell Has Something in Store for J.J. McCarthy
articles.summary: When the Minnesota Vikings set the initial 53-man roster, many were taken aback by the fact that they kept four […]
articles.body:
When the Minnesota Vikings set the initial 53-man roster, many were taken aback by the fact that they kept four quarterbacks on the team. J.J. McCarthy 's place on the roster had come into question, as did Max Brosmer's.

Yet, since Brosmer, an undrafted free agent from 2025, has been let go, some are wondering if his departure could impact McCarthy's spot in Minnesota too. Now an NFL insider is sharing his intel.

Albert Breer Says Kevin O'Connell Isn't Done With J.J. McCarthy

Still just 23 years old, now the question turns to McCarthy's future in Minnesota. Head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't named who will be Kyler Murray 's backup. But the belief is that job will go to Carson Wentz rather than McCarthy.

Still, just because KOC may or may not have more trust in Wentz leading a high-powered passing attack than the inexperienced McCarthy, it doesn't mean the Vikings don't still believe in the kid.

In fact, Sports Illustrated's NFL insider Albert Breer reported on Monday night that he "gets the sense" that coach O'Connell isn't done with McCarthy.

"I have gotten the sense, for what it's worth, that Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell wants to keep working with J.J. McCarthy."

That makes sense. After all, O'Connell was part of the decision to trade up and make McCarthy the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and the Vikings have only seen him play 10 times.

That's just not enough to evaluate a young QB prospect, especially one selected in the first round. If anyone knows that, it's O'Connell, who has taken on a few former first-round reclamation projects himself.

With McCarthy still under contract through the 2027 season, it just doesn't quite make sense to throw in the towel right now. But that doesn't mean the Vikings won't evaluate their options.

Now, Week 1 can certainly provide some fireworks, as both teams get acclimated to the start of the season. Notre Dame will be without star running backs Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price in the backfield, while Wisconsin has Colton Joseph leading the way at quarterback.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany doesn’t close door on Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala for DFB-Pokal
articles.summary: Is Jamal Musiala going to play for FC Bayern on Wednesday?
articles.body:
Ahead of the DFB-Pokal match against VfL Osnabrück, Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany sounded optimistic that the team would get attacker Serge Gnabry back soon.

"Sometimes I also only get an update after the press conference. Serge Gnabry isn't in the squad, but Lennart Karl is back – he's had his first few minutes on the pitch, which is very good for us. As for Jamal Musiala, we're having daily discussions; we haven't had any today yet – then we'll make a decision. He's trained very well. It's a question of choosing the right moment; whether that's tomorrow, at the weekend or next week, I can't yet say," said Kompany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "We need to discuss (when he will be back) with Serge; he might be there this weekend [against Schalke] – I expect he'll make his first appearance in the next ten days."

In the midst of giving that update on Gnabry, Kompany dropped a bit of a bombshell in saying that Musiala has not been officially ruled out yet. Is this gamesmanship or has Musiala made great progress in the last few days?

Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ) checked in to provide an update and seemed to blow by the chance for Musiala to play on Wednesday vs. VfL Osnabrück:

Jamal Musiala is making a good impression again in training. On Monday, he went into duels with full force, showed strong finishing, participated fully in the entire session, and looked very happy. Nevertheless, his comeback will not be rushed. It remains to be seen whether he will be back in the squad for Schalke on Saturday.

articles.title: ‘The Cardinal Countdown: 5 Days Until Kickoff’
articles.summary: KEYJUAN BROWN #5 Height: 5’10” Weight: 215lb Position: RB Class: Senior Hometown: Anniston, AL Summary: There are a few guys on this countdown each year that...
articles.body:
Summary: There are a few guys on this countdown each year that are likely "deserving" of a few paragraphs' worth of info or accolades because of their level of play and overall contributions to the teams. Then there are guys who are worthy of it…but it's not even necessary. If you are a casual or a diehard, you know the name Keyjuan Brown at this point, and while he may not be RB1 with a bullet, he's deserving of RB1 praise and recognition for the way he has played the last couple of years. Keyjuan sat behind Jaws and Guerendo in 2023 as a freshman, and then watched the emergence of Isaac and Duke in 2024, taking on that backup role during the season. In both instances Keyjuan didn't pout, he put in work, and in 2024 he was still went for over two hundred yards and three touchdowns on just 47 carries. Then in 2025 it was supposed to be Isaac and Duke again, but Watson never could quite find his mojo and Isaac couldn't get healthy….enter Keyjuan.

Keyjuan played in ten games last year, the most of any running back in the room, and in those ten games went for over 700 yards on the ground, six touchdowns, and another 118 yards receiving. Keyjuan got to show just how good he was in the primary role, and teams across the country took notice, so much so he was basically out the door with a bag packed for Boise in December when the coaches (and maybe a few extra bills) convinced him to stay here, and be RB1A with his common namesake in 2026. If Keyjuan needs evidence that Brohm and Barclay can have success with split load management at running back, look no further than 2025, or 2024, or 2023, or even 2022 at Purdue with a couple guys getting close to 100 carries a piece. This can work, and has worked, and while Isaac is a great running back, having Keyjuan as his partner will benefit them both.

Summary: With less than a week until the season starts, there are still people walking around without the realization that the Cards went and snagged a 13 game starter from an Iowa defense that finished Top 4 in the Big Ten in Passing Defense, Scoring Defense, and Total Defense in 2025. The strong safety from Ypsilanti, MI is going to spend his final season in college away from Iowa, and hopefully helping Louisville bring home some hardware. "Is this heaven" said Koen. To which Brohm replied, "no…it's Cardinal Stadium".

A lesser man may seek an apology from Koen for forcing yours truly to watch multiple Iowa football games, but I actually loved checking out how their defense works, and how they used Koen in various formations. I was surprised to see him down in the box so much last year, but he had the quickness to play in the middle, outside coverage when needed, and to drop him back in "centerfield" to scope the offensive adjustments. If I'm being honest, I don't think Entringer (ENT-Ringer) is a top safety nationally, nor do I peg him as a top athlete on the defensive side of the ball, but after watching the tape its tough to argue that he just makes plays. While some of that is scouting and skill, and some of it is athleticism, I just kept picking up hints of "grit" and "determination" each time I saw him getting involved. From jumping over guys to make a tackle, to reading screens, to getting down in the mud on special teams, Koen is a do it all guy that will likely be the Cards starter at Safety this year. If I had to sum it all up, it's this play from the Big Ten Championship a couple years back where he missed a tackle, and then never quite on the play, saving a touchdown. That's the heart of guy who will do whatever it takes to help his team, and I'm glad to have him.

articles.title: Rumour Mongering: Minteh Camp Believe Liverpool Deal Still Possible
articles.summary: Despite interest in Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have signalled not to expect any major deadline day signings.
articles.body:
Over the final few weeks of the transfer window, Brighton and Gambia 22-year-old Yankuba Minteh emerged as a target for Liverpool to fill the gap on the right wing by the departure of Mohamed Salah and to help balance out the fact almost every current Liverpool attacker is most comfortable on the right.

With Brighton demanding at least £70M for a player whose end product so far in his career has been on the limited side, with a goal involvement just about every 350 minutes last season when Salah's number in a down year was 140 and the much maligned Cody Gakpo managed 240, the club moved on.

Add in strong signals on Monday that Liverpool didn't expect any further incomings and that they had rejected an £80M Manchester City bid for Gakpo and would head into the meat of the season with the Dutch 27-year-old helping to cover the right side, though, and that seemed to confirm the situation.

However, according to Gambian reports, the player and his camp continue to believe a deal is possible and are pushing for it, which would only happen if Brighton can be convinced to lower their valuation. We're inclined to think that realistically the deal isn't currently on. Still, it's one to keep an eye on.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Reveals True Feelings On Mitchell Robinson Joining Rival Celtics
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson remains close with Mitchell Robinson, but says his former teammate becomes an enemy whenever Boston faces New York.
articles.body:
Jalen Brunson does not plan on letting this New York Knicks and Boston Celtics rivalry hamper the relationship that he has already built with his former teammate Mitchell Robinson . But Brunson was sure to mention that principle certainly disappears when the two teams meet.

Robinson left the defending champion Knicks this offseason and signed a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the Celtics, one of their biggest rivals.

Speaking with Stefan Bondy of the New York Post , Brunson made it clear that he is happy Robinson got his next big opportunity, regardless of where it came from.

"Obviously, playing for a rival, and I know people want every team to hate each other. "But there are some people you really care for, and that's my guy. I'm happy for him. And now, whenever we play him, four times a year, he's not my friend that day."

That response perfectly captures the very complicated dynamic that has been created because of Robinson's move.

Robinson spent years next to Brunson in New York and became an important part of the Knicks' championship run. His numbers were never that great, but his rebounding, rim protection, and physicality gave the Knicks a valuable weapon in the frontcourt.

Last season, Robinson averaged 1.2 blocks per game, despite playing just less than 20 minutes per night. His size and athleticism made him a very dangerous lob threat, and he was one of the league's most disruptive offensive rebounders.

Now those same qualities will be working against Brunson and the Knicks.

Robinson's departure was very interesting, especially after he said that he did not want to leave the Knicks . Robinson explained this on social media, responding to his former teammate OG Anunoby .

"I tried, brother. I didn't want this to happen. Hopefully, the truth comes out at some point. I'm gonna miss you, big dawg! Keep being great."

The decision appeared to be really influenced by the New York Knicks' financial limitations.

After winning the 2026 NBA title, the Knicks already had an expensive roster and reportedly wanted to avoid the second tax apron. That left Robinson as one of the players the Knicks could not comfortably retain, despite his importance to the team.

His move to Boston added another layer to the rivalry. Josh Hart jokingly told Robinson, "Bag well deserved. You an op now though," after the Celtics deal became official.

Robinson later fired back at Hart on social media , showing how quickly former teammates have embraced the competitive side of the move.

Brunson, however, is taking a more cautious and measured approach.

He understands why fans want players from rival teams to genuinely hate each other, particularly when the Knicks and Celtics are involved. But years spent sharing a locker room and winning a championship together do not disappear just because Robinson changed uniforms.

But that does not mean Brunson plans to take it easy on him. Boston plans to use Robinson as part of its center rotation, potentially behind Neemias Queta , giving the Celtics another elite rebounder and rim protector.

The Knicks and Celtics will see each other four times during the regular season, and another playoff matchup is certainly possible.

For Brunson, the line is simple: Robinson is still family away from the court. Once the ball goes up against Boston, that friendship, however, is officially on hold.

articles.title: Sunderland, Spurs reach £25m agreement for Kevin Danso
articles.summary: Hold me closer, tiny Danso. Big Kev, the subject of much speculation and numerous falling dominos in yesterday’s penultimate day of the transfer window, is h...
articles.body:
Hold me closer, tiny Danso. Big Kev, the subject of much speculation and numerous falling dominos in yesterday's penultimate day of the transfer window, is heading UP NORF to Sunderland, initially on loan with a purchase obligation.

Danso's obligation fee is £25m which honestly is a good fee for a guy we spent £20m to purchase last season after an initial loan from Lens. Kevin hasn't made it clear exactly why he wanted out of Spurs and to a team that many are suggesting will regress, but it's not hard to figure out. He'll be a backup at Spurs this season and quite possibly a starter or rotation option at Sunderland, a club that's in the Europa League this season after overachieving significantly.

£25m isn't a lot in the context of the insane Premier League transfer prices we've seen this summer, but it's still a good deal and a small profit for a Spurs player that asked to be sold and was never a starter to begin with. Spurs are losing him and his aerial ability in front of goal, and that will hurt, but with the £7m addition of Tosin Adarabioyo (very likely) coming today, Spurs will at least have a full compliment of senior defenders that De Zerbi can choose from.
